input.statement: Compute the one-loop effective potential V_1(phi) of massless real scalar lambda*phi^4 theory with tree-level potential V_tree(phi) = lambda*phi^4/4! in d = 4 - 2*eps dimensions using the MS-bar renormalization scheme, and show that the one-loop renormalization group equation mu * d(V_tree + V_1)/dmu + beta(lambda) * dV_tree/dlambda = 0 holds at order lambda^2 (where derivatives are partial derivatives holding the other variables fixed, and the field anomalous dimension gamma_phi = O(lambda^2) drops out at O(lambda^2)). Conventions and assumptions: Euclidean signature, hbar = c = 1, real coupling lambda > 0, nonzero real background field phi != 0, field-dependent squared mass m^2 = V_tree''(phi) = lambda*phi^2/2 > 0, renormalization scale mu > 0 with factor mu^(2*eps) on the bare d-dimensional integral, and MS-bar subtraction of the (1/eps - gamma_E + ln(4*pi)) pole combination.

answer_key.domain: real lambda > 0, real phi != 0, m^2 = lambda*phi^2/2 > 0, real mu > 0, dimensional regularization parameter d = 4 - 2*eps as eps -> 0
assumptions: Euclidean signature with natural units hbar = c = 1
V_tree(phi) = lambda*phi^4/24 with real lambda > 0 and real phi != 0
m^2(phi) = V_tree''(phi) = lambda*phi^2/2 > 0
Renormalization scale mu > 0 with mu^(2*eps) on the bare d-dimensional integral and MS-bar subtraction of (1/eps - gamma_E + ln(4*pi))
Partial derivatives in the RG equation hold the remaining variables fixed; field anomalous dimension gamma_phi = O(lambda^2) contributes only at O(lambda^3)
Mass dimensions: [phi] = [m] = [mu] = mass^1, [lambda] = mass^0, [V] = mass^4

steps.description: Setup: Euclidean signature, hbar = c = 1, V_tree(phi) = lambda*phi^4/24, m^2 = lambda*phi^2/2 > 0, lambda > 0, phi != 0, mu > 0, d = 4 - 2*eps, and MS-bar conventions.
Record the one-loop effective potential trace-log formula V_1^(d)(phi) = (1/2) * mu^(2*eps) * integral d^d k / (2*pi)^d * ln(k^2 + m^2) without an attached source.
State the dimensionally regularized closed form V_1^(d) = I_d(m^2) = -(1/2) * mu^(2*eps) * Gamma(-d/2) / (4*pi)^(d/2) * (m^2)^(d/2) as the definition of V_1^(d) in d = 4 - 2*eps.

Auxiliary numeric quadrature check of the UV-convergent second m^2-derivative at d = 3, m = 1.3 (omitting mu^(2*eps), i.e., mu = 1): compare numerical quadrature of -(1/2) * (4*pi)/(2*pi)^3 * integral_0^inf k^2 / (k^2 + m^2)^2 dk against the analytic second m^2-derivative -1/(16*pi*m) = -0.015303359912682243824... from two separate runs, agreeing to >12 digits.
Laurent-expand I_d(m^2) at d = 4 - 2*eps through O(eps^0): I_d(m^2) = -m^4/(64*pi^2)*(1/eps - gamma_E + ln(4*pi)) + m^4/(64*pi^2)*(ln(m^2/mu^2) - 3/2) + O(eps).

Apply MS-bar subtraction of -m^4/(64*pi^2)*(1/eps - gamma_E + ln(4*pi)) to obtain V_1^MSbar(phi) = m^4/(64*pi^2)*(ln(m^2/mu^2) - 3/2) = lambda^2*phi^4/(256*pi^2)*(ln(lambda*phi^2/(2*mu^2)) - 3/2), checking series match, mass^4 dimensions, and phi -> -phi symmetry.
Record the one-loop beta-function beta(lambda) = 3*lambda^2/(16*pi^2) as an unacknowledged model assumption without an attached source.
Verify one-loop RG invariance to order lambda^2: mu * d(V_tree + V_1^MSbar)/dmu + beta(lambda) * dV_tree/dlambda = -lambda^2*phi^4/(128*pi^2) + (3*lambda^2/(16*pi^2))*(phi^4/24) = 0.

Final answer: V_1^MSbar(phi) = m^4/(64*pi^2)*(ln(m^2/mu^2) - 3/2) with m^2 = lambda*phi^2/2 (equivalently lambda^2*phi^4/(256*pi^2)*(ln(lambda*phi^2/(2*mu^2)) - 3/2)), satisfying one-loop RG invariance at O(lambda^2). Own check passes symbolically, but effective tier is Unchecked because the closure rests on s2 (Assumed by model), s3 (Unchecked), and s7 (Assumed by model).

input.statement: Compute the asymptotic expansion through order O(g^2) as g -> 0+ of the zero-dimensional quartic partition function Z(g) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} exp(-x^2/2 - g*x^4) dx and the reduced free energy F(g) = -ln(Z(g)/Z(0)), where Z(0) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} exp(-x^2/2) dx. Domain and assumptions: real integration variable x in (-infty, infty), real coupling g > 0 in the asymptotic limit g -> 0+.

answer_key.domain: real x in (-infty, infty), real coupling g > 0 in the asymptotic limit g -> 0+
assumptions: x is real over (-infty, infty)
g is real and strictly positive (g > 0), with expansion understood as a Poincare asymptotic series as g -> 0+
Z(0) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} exp(-x^2/2) dx = sqrt(2*pi)

steps.description: Setup: definitions of Z(g) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} exp(-x^2/2 - g*x^4) dx and F(g) = -ln(Z(g)/Z(0)) for real x in (-infty, infty) and real g > 0 as g -> 0+.
Evaluate the free Gaussian normalization Z(0) = sqrt(2*pi) and the even Gaussian moments <x^4>_0 = 3, <x^8>_0 = 105, and <x^12>_0 = 10395 via exact symbolic integration.

Compute the formal perturbative expansion through O(g^2) from the Gaussian moments: Z_formal(g)/Z(0) = 1 - g*<x^4>_0 + (g^2/2)*<x^8>_0 + O(g^3) = 1 - 3*g + (105/2)*g^2 + O(g^3), so Z_formal(g) = sqrt(2*pi)*(1 - 3*g + (105/2)*g^2 + O(g^3)).

Analytic Poincare asymptotic justification (prose review): for u = g*x^4 >= 0 (g > 0), Lagrange's Taylor remainder satisfies -u^3/6 <= exp(-u) - (1 - u + u^2/2) <= 0, so |Z(g)/Z(0) - (1 - 3*g + (105/2)*g^2)| <= (1/6)*<x^12>_0*g^3 = (3465/2)*g^3; hence the divergent formal series is a valid Poincare asymptotic expansion of Z(g) as g -> 0+.

Expand F(g) = -ln(Z(g)/Z(0)) = -ln(1 - 3*g + (105/2)*g^2 + O(g^3)) = 3*g - (105/2 - 9/2)*g^2 + O(g^3) = 3*g - 48*g^2 + O(g^3). Own check passes series_match (Verified); effective tier is lowered to Model agreed by s4.

Final answer: Z(g) = sqrt(2*pi)*(1 - 3*g + (105/2)*g^2 + O(g^3)), F(g) = 3*g - 48*g^2 + O(g^3) as g -> 0+. Own check is Verified (series_match); effective tier is Model agreed because the asymptotic validity for the integral rests on s4.

input.statement: For a 1D quantum harmonic oscillator with energy levels E_n = hbar*omega*(n + 1/2) for integer n = 0, 1, 2, ..., compute the canonical partition function Z(beta) = sum_{n=0}^{infty} exp(-beta*E_n), the mean energy <E> = -d(ln Z)/dbeta, and the dimensionless heat capacity C_V/k_B = -beta^2 * d<E>/dbeta in terms of x = beta*hbar*omega, and then derive the high-temperature expansion of C_V/k_B as x -> 0+ through order O(x^4). Domain and assumptions: real positive parameters beta > 0, hbar > 0, omega > 0, k_B > 0 (so x = beta*hbar*omega > 0).

answer_key.domain: real beta > 0, hbar > 0, omega > 0, k_B > 0; dimensionless x = beta*hbar*omega > 0, high-temperature limit x -> 0+
assumptions: Discrete non-degenerate spectrum E_n = hbar*omega*(n + 1/2) for integer n >= 0
beta > 0, hbar > 0, omega > 0, k_B > 0 are strictly positive reals
x = beta*hbar*omega > 0 so 0 < exp(-x) < 1 and the geometric series converges absolutely
Canonical relations <E> = -d(ln Z)/dbeta and C_V = -k_B * beta^2 * d<E>/dbeta

steps.description: Setup: spectrum E_n = hbar*omega*(n + 1/2) (n >= 0), real positive beta, hbar, omega, k_B, x = beta*hbar*omega > 0, and canonical definitions of Z(beta), <E>, and C_V/k_B.

Evaluate the convergent geometric series Z(beta) = exp(-beta*hbar*omega/2) * sum_{n=0}^{infty} exp(-n*beta*hbar*omega) = exp(-beta*hbar*omega/2) / (1 - exp(-beta*hbar*omega)) = 1 / (2*sinh(beta*hbar*omega/2)).
Compute the mean energy <E> = -d(ln Z)/dbeta = (hbar*omega/2) * coth(beta*hbar*omega/2) = hbar*omega*(1/2 + 1/(exp(beta*hbar*omega) - 1)).
Compute the dimensionless heat capacity C_V/k_B = -beta^2 * d<E>/dbeta = (beta*hbar*omega / (2*sinh(beta*hbar*omega/2)))^2 = (x / (2*sinh(x/2)))^2 with x = beta*hbar*omega > 0.

Expand C_V/k_B = (x / (2*sinh(x/2)))^2 as x -> 0+ through O(x^4): C_V/k_B = 1 - x^2/12 + x^4/240 + O(x^6), verifying the classical equipartition limit C_V/k_B -> 1 as x -> 0+ and quantum freeze-out C_V/k_B -> 0 as x -> infty.
Final answer with x = beta*hbar*omega > 0: Z(beta) = 1/(2*sinh(x/2)), <E> = (hbar*omega/2)*coth(x/2), and C_V/k_B = (x/(2*sinh(x/2)))^2 = 1 - x^2/12 + x^4/240 + O(x^6).

input.statement: Evaluate the 3D massless boson energy-density integral I = integral_0^{infty} x^3 / (exp(x) - 1) dx exactly in closed form, and include an independent high-precision numerical quadrature cross-check to 50 decimal digits. Domain and assumptions: real integration variable x in (0, infty); you are given the Riemann zeta value zeta(4) = sum_{k=1}^{infty} 1/k^4 = pi^4/90.

assumptions: Real integration domain x in (0, infty) where exp(x) > 1 and 0 < exp(-x) < 1
Given zeta(4) = sum_{k=1}^{infty} 1/k^4 = pi^4/90

steps.description: Setup: integral I = integral_0^{infty} x^3 / (exp(x) - 1) dx on x in (0, infty), with zeta(4) = sum_{k=1}^{infty} 1/k^4 = pi^4/90 given.
For x > 0, use 0 < exp(-x) < 1 to expand the geometric series 1/(exp(x) - 1) = exp(-x)/(1 - exp(-x)) = sum_{k=1}^{infty} exp(-k*x), so x^3/(exp(x) - 1) = sum_{k=1}^{infty} x^3*exp(-k*x).

Analytic interchange (prose review): since x^3*exp(-k*x) > 0 for every x in (0, infty) and integer k >= 1, Tonelli's theorem justifies interchanging integral and sum: I = sum_{k=1}^{infty} integral_0^{infty} x^3*exp(-k*x) dx.
Evaluate each term symbolically for integer k >= 1: integral_0^{infty} x^3 * exp(-k*x) dx = Gamma(4)/k^4 = 6/k^4.

Combine s3 and s4 and sum over k >= 1 using given zeta(4) = pi^4/90: I = sum_{k=1}^{infty} 6/k^4 = 6*zeta(4) = 6*(pi^4/90) = pi^4/15. Own check is Verified; effective tier is lowered to Model agreed by Tonelli step s3.

Auxiliary non-blocking 50-digit numeric quadrature cross-check: mpmath.quad of x^3/expm1(x) on [0, inf] yields 6.4939394022668291490960221792470074166485057115124, agreeing with pi^4/15 to >50 decimal digits.

Final answer: I = pi^4/15, resting on the symbolic-plus-Tonelli derivation s5 (own check Verified, effective tier Model agreed because SymPy does not directly integrate x^3/(exp(x)-1) and the sum-integral interchange rests on prose step s3).

input.statement: Evaluate the parameter-dependent improper integral I(a) = integral_0^{infty} ln(1 + a^2 * x^2) / (1 + x^2) dx in closed form for real a > 0 via Feynman differentiation under the integral sign, explain explicitly why the assumption a > 0 matters (for general real a, I(a) = pi*ln(1 + |a|)), and include a separate 50-digit numerical quadrature cross-check across 12 positive values of a. Domain and assumptions: real integration variable x in (0, infty) and strictly positive real parameter a > 0.

answer_key.domain: real x in (0, infty), real parameter a > 0 (for general real a, I(a) = pi*ln(1 + |a|))
assumptions: Real integration variable x in (0, infty)

Strictly positive real parameter a > 0 (necessary because the integrand depends only on a^2 so I(a) = pi*ln(1 + |a|) for general real a, and in the Feynman derivative integral_0^infty dx/(1 + a^2*x^2) = pi/(2*|a|) = pi/(2*a) uses a > 0)

steps.description: Setup: I(a) = integral_0^{infty} ln(1 + a^2*x^2)/(1 + x^2) dx on x in (0, infty) with real a > 0, noting evenness I(-a) = I(a) so general real a yields pi*ln(1 + |a|).

Analytic Leibniz/DCT justification (prose review): I(0) = 0 with right-continuity lim_{a -> 0+} I(a) = 0 by dominated convergence (0 <= ln(1 + a^2*x^2)/(1 + x^2) <= ln(1 + x^2)/(1 + x^2) in L^1(0, infty) for 0 <= a <= 1), and differentiation under the integral sign is valid on every compact [a_min, a_max] subset (0, infty) via the L^1 bound |d/da integrand| <= 2*a_max/(a_min^2*(1 + x^2)).

Differentiate the integrand symbolically and evaluate integral_0^{infty} 2*a*x^2/((1 + x^2)*(1 + a^2*x^2)) dx for a > 0: partial fractions for a != 1 give (2*a/(a^2 - 1))*(pi/2 - pi/(2*a)) = pi/(1 + a) (where integral_0^{infty} dx/(1 + a^2*x^2) = pi/(2*a) uses a > 0), and direct evaluation at a = 1 gives pi/2 = pi/(1 + 1).

Integrate I'(t) = pi/(1 + t) from t = 0 to t = a > 0 using I(0+) = I(0) = 0 (s2) to obtain I(a) = pi*ln(1 + a). Own check is Verified; effective tier is lowered to Model agreed by the analytic Leibniz/DCT step s2.

Auxiliary non-blocking 50-digit numeric quadrature cross-check across 12 positive values a in {0.1, 0.25, 0.5, 0.75, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0, 3.0, 5.0, 7.5, 10.0, 25.0}: mpmath.quad agrees with pi*ln(1 + a) to >50 digits at all 12 points.
Final answer: I(a) = pi*ln(1 + a) for real a > 0 (and pi*ln(1 + |a|) for general real a). Own check is Verified; effective tier is Model agreed resting on s2.

input.statement: Find the closed form of the 2x2 matrix exponential U = exp(-i * theta * (n_x*sigma_x + n_y*sigma_y + n_z*sigma_z)) for a real parameter theta in R and a real unit vector n = (n_x, n_y, n_z) in R^3 satisfying n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2 = 1, where sigma_x, sigma_y, sigma_z are the Pauli matrices and I is the 2x2 identity matrix. Verify that U^dagger * U = I and det(U) = 1.

answer_key.domain: theta in R; n = (n_x, n_y, n_z) in R^3 with n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2 = 1
assumptions: theta is real (theta in R)
n_x, n_y, n_z are real (n in R^3)
unit-vector normalization n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2 = 1 (without |n| = 1, theta scales by |n| and A^2 = |n|^2*I != I)
standard Pauli matrices sigma_x = [[0, 1], [1, 0]], sigma_y = [[0, -i], [i, 0]], sigma_z = [[1, 0], [0, -1]] and 2x2 identity I
reality of theta and n is required for Hermiticity of n.sigma and unitarity U^dagger * U = I

steps.description: Declare the 2x2 identity I, the Pauli matrices sigma_x, sigma_y, sigma_z, real theta in R, real unit vector n = (n_x, n_y, n_z) in R^3 with n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2 = 1, and generator A = n_x*sigma_x + n_y*sigma_y + n_z*sigma_z.
Verify symbolically that A^2 = (n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2)*I = I under n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2 = 1, tr(A) = 0, and A^dagger = A under real n_x, n_y, n_z.

Sum the matrix exponential U = exp(-i*theta*A) using A^(2m) = I and A^(2m+1) = A to obtain U = cos(theta)*I - i*sin(theta)*A, verified symbolically against dU/dtheta = -i*A*U with U(0) = I and exact spherical-coordinate Matrix.exp().

Verify SU(2) group properties symbolically under real theta, n and n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2 = 1: U^dagger * U = (cos^2(theta) + sin^2(theta)*(n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2))*I = I and det(U) = cos^2(theta) + sin^2(theta)*(n_x^2 + n_y^2 + n_z^2) = 1.
Conclude U = cos(theta)*I - i*sin(theta)*(n_x*sigma_x + n_y*sigma_y + n_z*sigma_z), satisfying U^dagger * U = I and det(U) = 1 on the stated domain.

input.statement: Compute the retarded Green's function G_R(t) of the strictly underdamped harmonic oscillator satisfying (d^2/dt^2 + 2*gamma*d/dt + omega_0^2) G_R(t) = delta(t) on t in R, subject to causality G_R(t) = 0 for t < 0 and jump conditions G_R(0+) = 0, G_R'(0+) = 1, in the strictly underdamped regime 0 < gamma < omega_0. Express G_R(t) in closed form using the Heaviside step function Theta(t) and explain why 0 < gamma < omega_0 selects the oscillatory form with Omega = sqrt(omega_0^2 - gamma^2) > 0.

answer_key.domain: t in R; real gamma, omega_0 with 0 < gamma < omega_0 (so Omega = sqrt(omega_0^2 - gamma^2) > 0)
assumptions: t is real (t in R)
gamma and omega_0 are real with 0 < gamma < omega_0 (strictly underdamped regime)

0 < gamma < omega_0 makes both 0 < gamma (strict exponential decay exp(-gamma*t) -> 0, excluding the undamped gamma = 0 boundary) and 4*(gamma^2 - omega_0^2) < 0 (strictly negative characteristic discriminant), selecting complex-conjugate roots -gamma +- i*Omega with real frequency Omega = sqrt(omega_0^2 - gamma^2) > 0 and oscillatory sin(Omega*t)/Omega rather than critical t*exp(-gamma*t) or overdamped sinh(kappa*t)/kappa
retarded causality boundary condition G_R(t) = 0 for t < 0
jump conditions G_R(0+) = 0 and G_R'(0+) = 1 induced by the unit Dirac delta source delta(t)

steps.description: State the defining distributional ODE (d^2/dt^2 + 2*gamma*d/dt + omega_0^2) G_R(t) = delta(t), causality G_R(t) = 0 for t < 0, jump conditions G_R(0+) = 0 and G_R'(0+) = 1, and strictly underdamped parameters 0 < gamma < omega_0 with Omega = sqrt(omega_0^2 - gamma^2) > 0.

Solve the homogeneous characteristic equation r^2 + 2*gamma*r + omega_0^2 = 0 for t > 0: since 0 < gamma < omega_0, the discriminant is -4*Omega^2 < 0, giving roots r_+- = -gamma +- i*Omega and real oscillatory solution g(t) = exp(-gamma*t)*(C_1*cos(Omega*t) + C_2*sin(Omega*t)).
Apply the jump conditions at t = 0+: g(0+) = C_1 = 0 and g'(0+) = -gamma*C_1 + Omega*C_2 = 1 give C_1 = 0 and C_2 = 1/Omega, so g(t) = exp(-gamma*t)*sin(Omega*t)/Omega for t > 0.

Verify symbolically that (d^2/dt^2 + 2*gamma*d/dt + omega_0^2) g(t) = 0 for t > 0, g(0+) = 0, g'(0+) = 1 (hence distributional operator on Theta(t)*g(t) yields delta(t)), and verify exact Laplace transform L{g}(s) = 1/(s^2 + 2*gamma*s + omega_0^2).

Substitute Omega = sqrt(omega_0^2 - gamma^2) and multiply by Theta(t) to obtain G_R(t) = Theta(t)*exp(-gamma*t)*sin(sqrt(omega_0^2 - gamma^2)*t)/sqrt(omega_0^2 - gamma^2), cross-checking the critical-damping limit Omega -> 0+ gives Theta(t)*t*exp(-gamma*t).

Characteristic roots, jump conditions, homogeneous ODE residual, Laplace transform 1/(s^2 + 2*gamma*s + omega_0^2), and critical-damping limit Omega -> 0+ verified symbolically in SymPy using omega_0 = sqrt(gamma^2 + Omega^2) with gamma > 0, Omega > 0. input.statement: Evaluate the definite integral I(a, b) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} dx / ((x^2 + a^2)*(x^2 + b^2)) for real parameters a > 0 and b > 0, covering both a != b and the degenerate limit b -> a+ (giving I(a, a) = pi/(2*a^3)). Explicitly state how the positivity assumptions a > 0, b > 0 determine the pole locations and remove absolute-value or sign ambiguities.

answer_key.domain: a > 0, b > 0 (real strictly positive parameters, covering both a != b and a = b)
assumptions: a and b are real and strictly positive (a > 0, b > 0)

because the integrand depends only on a^2 and b^2, for general nonzero real a, b the value is pi/(|a|*|b|*(|a| + |b|)); positivity a > 0, b > 0 places the upper-half-plane poles strictly at z = +i*a and z = +i*b and eliminates absolute values and sign ambiguities
the integral diverges if a = 0 or b = 0, and converges absolutely for all real a > 0, b > 0 since the integrand decays as O(x^-4) as |x| -> infty

steps.description: State I(a, b) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} dx / ((x^2 + a^2)*(x^2 + b^2)) with real a > 0, b > 0, noting absolute convergence (O(x^-4) decay) and upper-half-plane poles at z = i*a and z = i*b.

For a != b, verify the partial-fraction identity 1/((x^2 + a^2)*(x^2 + b^2)) = (1/(b^2 - a^2))*(1/(x^2 + a^2) - 1/(x^2 + b^2)) and locate the two simple upper-half-plane poles z = i*a and z = i*b using a > 0, b > 0.

Evaluate I(a, b) for a != b by summing upper-half-plane residues 2*pi*i*(Res_{z=i*a} + Res_{z=i*b}) = 2*pi*i*(i/(2*a*(a^2 - b^2)) - i/(2*b*(a^2 - b^2))) = pi/(a*b*(a + b)), cross-checked by integrating the partial fractions with integral_{-infty}^{infty} dx/(x^2 + c^2) = pi/c for c > 0.

Verify the degenerate case b = a > 0: the continuous limit lim_{b -> a+} pi/(a*b*(a + b)) = pi/(2*a^3) agrees exactly with the double-pole residue 2*pi*i * Res_{z=i*a} 1/(z^2 + a^2)^2 = pi/(2*a^3) and direct integration of integral_{-infty}^{infty} dx/(x^2 + a^2)^2.
Conclude that I(a, b) = pi/(a*b*(a + b)) holds uniformly for all real a > 0, b > 0 (both a != b and a = b), verified against direct SymPy integration.

input.statement: Evaluate the Laplace transform L(s, a) = integral_0^{infty} exp(-s*t) * J_0(a*t) dt for real s > 0 and all real a in R (covering both |a| < s and |a| >= s), where J_0 is the Bessel function of the first kind of order zero. assumptions: s is real and strictly positive (s > 0), guaranteeing absolute exponential convergence since |J_0(a*t)| <= 1 for all real a*t
a is real (a in R), covering both the restricted disc |a| < s and the exterior |a| >= s where s^2 + a^2 > 0 makes the positive real square root sqrt(s^2 + a^2) unambiguous

term-by-term integration of J_0(a*t) = sum_{k=0}^{infty} (-1)^k*(a*t/2)^(2k)/(k!)^2 yields the binomial series (1/s)*sum_{k=0}^{infty} binomial(-1/2, k)*(a^2/s^2)^k, which converges absolutely (justifying term-by-term Fubini-Tonelli integration) on |a| < s, converges only conditionally at |a| = s (where absolute convergence fails), and diverges for |a| > s

Verify exact Taylor-series agreement between the term-by-term integrated Bessel series and the expansion of 1/sqrt(s^2 + a^2) in a around 0 to O(a^14) (even powers through a^12) on |a| < s, noting that the series radius of convergence is |a| = s and it diverges for |a| > s.

steps: Rewrite x^2 - 4*x + 4 = (x - 2)^2, so f(x) = sqrt((x - 2)^2) + x for all x in [0, 4].

input.statement: Check the following 4-step derivation computing the fourth Gaussian moment I_4(alpha) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} x^4 * exp(-alpha*x^2) dx for real alpha > 0 by integration by parts starting from I_0(alpha) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} exp(-alpha*x^2) dx = sqrt(pi/alpha).
steps: Take the standard Gaussian integral I_0(alpha) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} exp(-alpha*x^2) dx = sqrt(pi/alpha) for real alpha > 0.

Integrate I_2(alpha) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} x * (x * exp(-alpha*x^2)) dx by parts with u = x and dv = x*exp(-alpha*x^2) dx (so v = -exp(-alpha*x^2)/(2*alpha)); the boundary term vanishes as |x| -> infty for alpha > 0, giving I_2(alpha) = I_0(alpha)/(2*alpha) = sqrt(pi)/(2*alpha^(3/2)).

Integrate I_4(alpha) = integral_{-infty}^{infty} x^3 * (x * exp(-alpha*x^2)) dx by parts with u = x^3 and dv = x*exp(-alpha*x^2) dx (so v = -exp(-alpha*x^2)/(2*alpha)); the boundary term vanishes as |x| -> infty for alpha > 0, obtaining I_4(alpha) = (3/alpha)*I_2(alpha).

Substitute I_2(alpha) = sqrt(pi)/(2*alpha^(3/2)) from step 2 into the step-3 expression J_4(alpha) = (3/alpha)*I_2(alpha): J_4(alpha) = (3/alpha)*(sqrt(pi)/(2*alpha^(3/2))) = 3*sqrt(pi)/(2*alpha^(5/2)).

assumptions: alpha is real with alpha > 0
x is real integrated over (-infty, infty)

steps.description: State the standard Gaussian integral I_0(alpha) = sqrt(pi/alpha) for alpha > 0.
Compute I_2(alpha) = I_0(alpha)/(2*alpha) = sqrt(pi)/(2*alpha^(3/2)) by integration by parts with vanishing boundary terms for alpha > 0.

Planted error: dropped factor of 1/2 in integration by parts of I_4(alpha), claiming (3/alpha)*I_2(alpha) instead of the exact relation (3/(2*alpha))*I_2(alpha). At alpha = 1, I_4(1) = 3*sqrt(pi)/4 while 3*I_2(1) = 3*sqrt(pi)/2 (residual -3*sqrt(pi)/4).

Substitute I_2(alpha) = sqrt(pi)/(2*alpha^(3/2)) into (3/alpha)*I_2(alpha) to get 3*sqrt(pi)/(2*alpha^(5/2)). Locally exact substitution given s3, but effective tier is Failed via S2 broken-closure propagation from s3 (displayed as 'Broken: rests on failed s3').

input.statement: Prove that for any Hermitian linear operator H = H^dagger on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space (V, <.,.>) (where the inner product is antilinear in the first argument, linear in the second argument, and positive definite: <v, v> > 0 for all nonzero v in V), (1) every eigenvalue of H is real, and (2) eigenvectors corresponding to distinct eigenvalues are orthogonal.

answer_key.final_answer: For any Hermitian operator H = H^dagger on a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space (V, <.,.>), every eigenvalue lambda is real (lambda = conj(lambda)) and eigenvectors for distinct eigenvalues lambda != mu are orthogonal (<u, v> = 0).
assumptions: (V, <.,.>) is a finite-dimensional complex inner-product space
<.,.> is antilinear in the first argument, linear in the second argument, and positive definite (<v, v> > 0 for v != 0)
H: V -> V is linear and Hermitian (H = H^dagger), meaning <H u, v> = <u, H v> for all u, v in V

steps.description: State the inner-product space axioms (antilinearity in the first argument, linearity in the second, positive definiteness) and the Hermiticity hypothesis <H u, v> = <u, H v>.
Reality of eigenvalues: for H v = lambda v with v != 0, lambda <v, v> = <v, H v> = <H v, v> = conj(lambda) <v, v>; since <v, v> > 0, (lambda - conj(lambda)) = 0, so lambda is real.

Orthogonality for distinct eigenvalues: for H u = lambda u and H v = mu v with lambda != mu, reality from s2 gives mu <u, v> = <u, H v> = <H u, v> = conj(lambda) <u, v> = lambda <u, v>, so (mu - lambda) <u, v> = 0 and hence <u, v> = 0.

answer_key.domain: finite-dimensional complex inner-product space (V, <.,.>) and Hermitian linear operator H = H^dagger

input.statement: Prove that there are infinitely many prime numbers p congruent to 3 (mod 4). Explicitly assume standard integer arithmetic and the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (every integer n >= 2 factors into a finite product of primes).

answer_key.final_answer: There are infinitely many prime numbers p congruent to 3 (mod 4).
assumptions: Standard integer arithmetic and modular congruence modulo 4
Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic: every integer n >= 2 factors into a finite product of primes

steps.description: State standard integer arithmetic hypotheses and the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (every integer n >= 2 factors into primes).
Auxiliary algebraic closure lemma: for integers a, b, (4*a + 1)*(4*b + 1) = 4*(4*a*b + a + b) + 1, showing closure of the residue class 1 (mod 4) under multiplication.
Assume finitely many primes p_1, ..., p_k == 3 (mod 4) (k >= 1, with p_1 = 3), and set N = 4*p_1*...*p_k - 1 >= 11. Show N is odd, N == 3 (mod 4), and gcd(N, p_i) = 1 for every i in {1, ..., k}.

By the Fundamental Theorem of Arithmetic (s1), N >= 11 factors into odd primes (each 1 or 3 mod 4). By induction using s2, a product solely of primes == 1 (mod 4) is == 1 (mod 4), contradicting N == 3 (mod 4) from s3. Hence N has a prime factor q == 3 (mod 4) outside {p_1, ..., p_k}, a contradiction. Effective tier is min(Model agreed, Verified, Model agreed) = Model agreed (skipping neutral Given s1).

answer_key.domain: integers Z and positive prime numbers p >= 2
